title: B1-03 · The active and passive participle

blocks.text: B1-03 · The active and passive participle
Lesson overview

Participle is the most versatile word in Arabic. The same ⁧اسْمُ الفَاعِلِ⁩ (active participle) may be an adjective ('the responsible official'), a name ('the responsible person') almost a verb at present ('I am going'), and holds a complement like a verb; the same applies to ⁧اسْمُ المَفْعُولِ⁩ (passive participle). In the newspapers, participants are everywhere: ⁧المُشَارِكُونَ⁩ , ⁧المُتَّهَمُ⁩ , ⁧المُتَوَقَّعُ⁩ , ⁧المَسْمُوحُ بِهِ⁩ . In this unit you learn to form them from all forms, to recognize active and passive without vowels and to use them in their four roles. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 100–101), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, dictionary by root, Grammar G43, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. form the active and passive participle of each form, including the most frequent cases with weak roots;
2. use the participle as an adjective, as a name and with verbal value (present state, imminent action);
3. build the passive participle of verbs with preposition ( ⁧مَسْمُوحٌ بِهِ⁩ , ⁧مُتَّفَقٌ عَلَيْهِ⁩ );
4. form the female and plural participles, healthy and over;
5. to distinguish active and passive participle in a text without vowels thanks to context;
6. translate the participles into English with the most natural form (relative, adjective, name, gerund).
Two-week plan.

The rule for derived forms (B1-02): take the imperfect, replace the prefix with ⁧مُـ⁩ ; with the first of the last radical you have the asset, with the a the passive: ⁧يُنَظِّمُ⁩ → ⁧مُنَظِّم⁩ / ⁧مُنَظَّم⁩ . When the passive is missing. Intransitional verbs ( ⁧تَطَوَّعَ⁩ , ⁧اِنْسَحَبَ⁩ , ⁧اِسْتَقَلَّ⁩ ) do not have a simple passive participle: they have at most the one with preposition (section 6).
3. Participants of weak roots (recognize)
You will study them thoroughly in B1-06; In the meantime, he learns to recognize the most frequent forms.

Two rules to remember. 1. In the active participle of form I of concave verbs the weak letter becomes hamza: ⁧قَائِل⁩ , ⁧عَائِد⁩ . 2. The active participle of defects loses the ⁧ي⁩ Without Article: ⁧قَاضٍ⁩ A judge shall be the same, but ⁧القَاضِي⁩ The judge is the judge.

6. Participle as a verb: what time does it express?
The participle does not have its own time: it expresses a state or action seen in its course or outcome. The Italian translation depends on the verb.

rows: ⁧هِيَ مُحْضِرَةٌ الأَوْرَاقَ⁩ He brought the documents (and he has them with him)

blocks.text: In the formal written language this verbal use is less frequent than in the spoken language: in newspapers the participle appears mainly as an adjective and as a name. In the spoken language, and in the Egyptian, it is very frequent (A2-23: ʿāyiz, sākin, fāhim).
7. The passive participle with preposition
If the verb holds a preposition ( ⁧سَمَحَ بِـ⁩ , ⁧اِتَّفَقَ عَلَى⁩ , ⁧شَكَّ فِي⁩ ), the passive participle is invariant and carries the preposition with a pronoun that accords with the name.

8. Female and plural

Practical rules. Participles of derived forms ( ⁧مُـ⁩ ) they almost always take the healthy plural: ⁧مُوَظَّفُونَ⁩ , ⁧مُتَطَوِّعُونَ⁩ . Participants of Form Used as trade or category names often have a plural over ( ⁧كُتَّاب⁩ , ⁧عُمَّال⁩ , ⁧تُجَّار⁩ ); used as adjectives, the healthy plural. The passive participles referring to things take ⁧ـات⁩ or a plural over
( ⁧مَشَارِيعُ⁩ ).
9. Active or passive without vowels?
In active and passive derived forms the same are written: ⁧مرسل⁩ , ⁧مستقبل⁩ , ⁧محتل⁩ , ⁧منظم⁩ . Decide with three questions:

1. Person or what? A person doing the action → active: ⁧المُنَظِّمُونَ⁩ The organisers are the organizers. Something that suffer → passive: ⁧مَعْرِضٌ مُنَظَّمٌ جَيِّدًا⁩ It's a well-organized exhibition.
2. Is there a complement? A direct or in iḍāfa → Active: ⁧مُرْسِلُ الرِّسَالَةِ⁩ The sender of the letter is the same as the sender.

3. What does the rest of the sentence say? ⁧المُسْتَقْبَلُ القَرِيبُ⁩ • the near future (passive, fixed) · ⁧المُسْتَقْبِلُونَ⁩ Those receiving (asset). Watch out for the couples in the news. ⁧المُتَّهَمُ⁩ The defendant, the accused (passive) / ⁧المُتَّهِمُ⁩ • the accuser (active, rare); ⁧الأَرَاضِي المُحْتَلَّةُ⁩ The occupied territories (passive) / ⁧المُحْتَلُّ⁩ • the overweight (active). A vowel changes who does and who suffers: in a translation it is a serious mistake.
10. Pronunciation

I'm the decisive one. Try to pronounce the couples clearly: munaẓẓim / munaẓẓam, mursil / mursal, mustaqbil / mustaqbal. The tutor says one of the two words, you say whether it's active or passive. The concave hamza. qāʾil, ʿāʾid, bāʾiʿ: the hamza between the two vowels must be pronounced, with a small detachment, not as a y (*qāyil is Egyptian, not fuṣḥā).
